Common Hepatology Billing Problems

Liver biopsy imaging guidance add-on not billed when ultrasound guidance was used.

Complex cirrhosis management visit coded at low E/M level when MDM supports high complexity.

Post-transplant management visits billed to wrong payer or with wrong provider type.

PMEX confirms the correct payer structure and provider type for post-transplant management billing.

NASH diagnosis coded as unspecified fatty liver, losing specificity-based reimbursement differences.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Hepatology Billing

Hepatology practices lose 16 to 26 percent of revenue to antiviral authorization gaps, elastography coverage failures, and E/M under-coding.

PATTERN 01

HCV Antiviral Denied, Step Therapy Not Met

Patient prescribed ledipasvir/sofosbuvir. Commercial payer requires documentation of genotype, fibrosis staging, and absence of prior treatment contraindications. Authorization submitted without the genotype result. Denied. Drug cost: $24,000 per course.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX compiles the complete prior authorization package for DAA therapy before submission, including genotype result, FibroScan or biopsy fibrosis stage, prior treatment history, and prescribing hepatologist documentation.

PATTERN 02

FibroScan Denied, Diagnosis Not Covered

Liver elastography (91200) billed for a patient with elevated liver enzymes. Payer LCD requires a specific chronic liver disease diagnosis such as chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, or NAFLD with fibrosis. Elevated enzymes alone do not qualify. Claim denied.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms the diagnosis code against the applicable LCD before billing elastography. When the ordering diagnosis needs to be more specific, PMEX flags the order before the procedure is billed.

PATTERN 03

Cirrhosis Visit Under-Coded

Patient with decompensated cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and ascites. All three complications managed at the visit. Billed as 99214 (moderate complexity). Correct: 99215 (high complexity). Multiple chronic conditions with acute decompensation support high complexity MDM.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes hepatology E/M from 2021 MDM criteria, evaluating the number and severity of conditions managed, data reviewed, and risk of management. Decompensated cirrhosis with active complications consistently supports high-complexity coding.

Questions

Hepatology Billing Questions Answered

Most payers require HCV genotype, fibrosis stage (FibroScan result or liver biopsy), prior treatment history, and the prescribing hepatologist documentation. We compile this package before submitting the authorization.

Liver elastography is billed with CPT 91200. It requires a covered chronic liver disease diagnosis and is separately billable from the office visit. We confirm LCD coverage before billing.

Yes. Ultrasound guidance (76942) is separately billable when documented in the procedure note alongside the liver biopsy CPT code (47000).

Post-transplant management is billed under the transplant center and treating hepatologist with the correct provider type, payer structure, and transplant-specific diagnosis codes. We confirm the billing framework at the start of engagement.

NAFLD is coded as K76.0 (fatty change of liver). NASH is coded as K75.81. Fibrosis stage is documented in the clinical note and reflected in the coding for procedures like FibroScan and liver biopsy. We apply the most specific code the documentation supports.
